sentences.text: *J U D G M E N T*

This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioner U/S 166 of M.V. Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by him, in a road traffic accident.

*FACTS OF THE CASE IN NUTSHELL*

sentences.text:
Facts leading to the case of the petitioner forthcoming in the petition that, on 24.05.2022 at about 2.30 a.m. the petitioner was proceeding in a Motor cycle bearing registration No. KA-40-EE- 7152 slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road, at Teneyuru Dinne on Sidlaghatta-Hosakote Road,
Sulibele Hobli, Hosakote Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District.

At that time, driver of the Maruthi Swift Car bearing registration No. KA.50-MB- 2587, came from the same direction, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed violently against the vehicle of the petitioner, to its rear side.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained 3.
It is further stated that, immediately the petitioner was shifted to MVJ Medical college and research Hospital Hosakote.
Thereafter, to Gourav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital.
Due to the injuries sustained by the petitioner, became physically and functionally disabled, in spite of taking treatment.
The petitioner had spent a lot towards medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment.

4. It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 23 years, doing Mason work and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month, and he used to spend the said amount, for the maintenance of his family members.
After the accident, he could not do any work due to his severe injuries.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-50-MB-2587.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Wilson Garden Traffic Police as per Crime No.43/2022 under section 279 and 337 of IPC.
As such, the respondent No.1, being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
6. After registration of the case, as usual notices were issued to the respondents.
In response to the notices, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court, remained absent, placed exparte.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement in answer to the case of the petitioner.
7. In the written statement of the respondent No.2, has not seriously disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

But, seriously disputed the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car, contending that, due to the sole negligence on the part of the petitioner, alleged accident and its consequences were taken place.
At the same time, admitted about the issuance of policy in connection with the offending vehicle, and the same was valid as on the date of accident, subject to its terms and conditions.

It is another contention of the respondent that, the driver had no valid and effective driving license to drive the said vehicle, and the owner of the offending vehicle had no valid vehicle documents as on the date of the accident.
Ultimately stated that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner, is highly excessive, exorbitant and without any basis.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.
8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, for final determination of the case, following issues are framed;
Naveen

*ISSUES*
1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident,
that was taken place on 24.05.2022 at about 2,30 a.m near Teneyuru Dinne, Hosakote- Sidlaghatta Road, Sulibele Hobli, Bengaluru Rural District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the CAR bearing registration No.KA-50-MB-2587, in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom?
3) What order or award?

9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner by name Naveen Kumar B.V, during the course of evidence, placed his affidavit evidence, in lieu of examination-in-chief, who examined as PW1 in the case on hand.
At the time of his evidence, 14 documentary evidence got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.
In addition this, placed the evidence of PW2- Dr. S.A Somashekara.
At the time of the evidence of this witness, two documents got marked at Ex.P.15 and Ex.P.16.
One more witness Record Keeper by name K. Srinivas examined as PW3.
At the time of his evidence documents marked as Ex.P.17 and Ex.P.18.
In addition to this, Dr.N. Chaitanya Babu, Dental surgeon examined as PW4.

At the time of his evidence, one document got marked as Ex.P.19.
10.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not adduced any rebuttal evidence in order to disprove the contention of the petitioner, and to prove all the defenses forthcoming in the written statement.
At the same time, it is pertinent to note that, the respondent No.1, being owner of the offending vehicle, remained silent, without challenging the case of the petitioner.

11. Heard the arguments of both the counsel, and perused the materials available on record.
12.

On appreciation of the evidence available on record, my findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:
*R E A S O N S* ISSUE NO.1:-

13. It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle Car, bearing registration No.KA-03-MB-2587 alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

14. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company, though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, seriously disputed the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, contending that, due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner, alleged accident, and its consequences were taken place.

But, not Naveen Kumar B.V vs Manjunatha.N on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190638738/
3 adduced any rebuttal evidence for consideration.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle has not appeared before the court, remained absent, placed exparte.
In such a situation, duty is more on the part of the court, to assess the evidence available on record, in order to come to the proper conclusion, in connection with the above fact in issue.
15. On going through the above issue, burden is on the petitioner, to prove the same, on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.

The petitioner- Naeen Kumar B.V to discharge the burden lies on him, relied on his affidavit evidence, wherein, he reiterated the main petition averments about the accident and injuries sustained by him consequent upon the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The affidavit evidence of the petitioner remained unquestioned.
On the other hand to prove all the defenses forthcoming in the written statement of the respondent company, not adduced any rebuttal evidence for consideration.
16. Among the documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner, Ex.P1 to Ex.P6 Ex.P14 are the material documents in support of the above issue.

Remaining documents and the evidence of PW2 to PW4 are to be discussed in detail, at the time of appreciation of evidence while coming to the conclusion in connection with the issue No.2.
17.

On taking birds eye view towards the documentary evidence, Ex.P1- first information report,
discloses that, alleged accident had taken place on 24.05.2022.
First information was given by the the brother of the petitoner by name Manohar B.V on 27.5.2022.

In connection with this inordinate delay of days in giving first information is concerned, it is noted in the column No.3(c) of Ex.P1 to the effect that, since the complainant was providng treatment to his brother/petitoner, belatted complaint was given.
The said reason also forthcomming in the complaint avermetns.
To disprove the said reasons, no contra materials availble on record, for consideration.
Apart form this to suspect about the case of the petitioner, no contra materials available on record, from the side of the respondents.
Added to this, it is pertinent to note that, when the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries consequent upon the accident, one cannot expect immediate complaint from the complainant.

As such, in the absence of the rebuttal evidence to disprove the reasons noted on the point of delay, and on appreciation of th entire medical documents, I am of th view that, the said point of delay is not fatal to the case of the petitioner, and on the said point, entire claim petition,
filed under beneficial legislation, cannot be thrown out.

18. Another material point forthcoming in the police papers that, on the basis of first information given by the complainant, criminal law set in motion against the driver of the offending vehicle,
alleging that, he had committed the offenses punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.

In the recitals of the complaint, and also in column No.10 of the Ex.P1, there is a clear narration about the actionable negligence said to have committed by the driver of the offending vehicle, as on the date of the accident.
Either the driver or its owner have not made an effort well in time before the competent court of law, to prove the innocence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Accordingly,
these two material documents which laid down the foundation remained unquestioned.

19. Added to this, Ex.P3- spot mahazar said to have executed in the presence of panch witnesses,
report of the motor vehicle inspector, ans wound certificate marked at Ex.P4 and Ex.P5, go to show Naveen Kumar B.V vs Manjunatha.N on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190638738/
4 about the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.
As per the report of the motor vehicle inspector, alleged accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles involved in the accident.
As per the wound certificates, on the history of RTA, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
All these material documents remained unquestioned by the other side.

The contents of the Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.5 give clear picture about the genuineness of the case of the petitioner, about the accident, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

20. Ultimately, on going through the charge sheet submitted by the investigation officer, as per Ex.P6 reveals that, after due investigation process final report has been filed against the driver of the offending vehicle by name Manjunatha on the allegation that, he had committed the offences punishable under section 279, and 338 of IPC.
The narration made in the column No.17 of the charge sheet remained unshaken.

No doubt, the final report is not substantive piece of evidence to consider the claim petition, but in the absence of contra materials and rebuttal evidence, there is no hurdle to believe the said document as conclusive proof in support of the above fact in issue.
Another document, Ex.P.14- police intimation also, supports the case of the petitioner.

21. Another point to be discussed herein that, at the time of cross-examination of PW1, though several questions put to the witness by the learned counsel for the respondent company, on the point of delay, about the accident spot, colour of the offending vehicle, manner of the accident,
nothing has been elicited to disbelieve the entire case of the petitioner, and to disbelieve the recitals of the police documents, and also to believe the defenses of the respondents, and to prove the innocence of the driver of the offending vehicle, as well as to prove that, due to the sole negligence on the part of the petitioner, alleged accident and its consequences were taken place.
Hence, I am of the view that, the petitioner herein, has placed satisfactory and convincing evidence, in support of the above fact in issue.
22. Overall appreciation of the evidence placed on record, I am of the view that, in support of the above issue, the petitioner has placed cogent and convincing evidence for consideration.

In the light of the evidence placed on record by the petitioner, in the case on hand, by way of affidavit and the documentary evidence, speak that, the alleged accident was occurred, due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle car bearing registration No.KA-50-MB-2587

Hence,
without making much discussion on the point of the rash and negligent riding of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the Issue No.1, is in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 :
23.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident, under different heads.

24. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.

Naveen Kumar B.V vs Manjunatha.N on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190638738/
5 Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another.

entities.text: Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.

"
25. In connection with the injuries sustained by the petitioner, in the accident, has produced wound certificate, marked as Ex.P5.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injury:-
1). Communited Fracture of right humerus at 1/3rd junction 2) Clavicular fracture of right side, mandibular fracture 26.
In connection with the above said injuries, the doctor is of the opinion that said injuries are grievous in nature.
Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summary, OPD records, medical bills, advance bills, prescriptions & x-rays as per Ex.P9 to Ex.P14.
In addition to his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.S.A.Somashekar PW2.
At the time of his evidence placed OPD record & x-ray as per Ex.P15 & Ex.P16.
Apart from this evidence plaed the evidence of K.Srinivas, Record Keeper at Gaurav Orthopaedic Hospital as PW3.
He has placed Case sheet along with authorisation letter as per Ex.P17 & Ex.P18.
Further examined Dr.N.Chaitanya Babu as PW4.
He has placed on ex-ray as per Ex.P19.
On going through the discharge summary of Gaurav Orthopaedic Hospital, Kolar marked at Ex.P9 goes to show that, the petitioner was admitted from 24.5.2022 to 3.6.2022.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as am in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation of Rs.70,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.
27. Another point to be discussed herein, about the loss of income during laid up period and rest period.
In the petition, he had stated that, he was doing Mason and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has not produced any iota of documents, to show his definite income per month, prior to the accident.
In such a situation, as per law, notional income has to be taken.
On going through the discharge summary of Gaurav Orthopaedic Hospital, Kolar marked at Ex.P9 goes to show that, the petitioner was admitted from 24.5.2022 to 3.6.2022.

During period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to him, to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of one month, by looking in to the nature of the injuries Naveen Kumar B.V vs Manjunatha.N on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190638738/
6 sustained, by him.

Hence, I am of the view that, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,500/-
towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

28. The petitioner herein, in connection with his treatment expenses, at the time of his evidence,
placed 51 medical bills of Rs.2,09,422/- as per Ex.P11.

At the time of cross-examination of PW1,
nothing has been elicted to disbelive the said medical bills.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,09,422/- towards medical expenses.

29. The petitioner herein, as per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summary of Gaurav Orthopaedic Hospital, Kolar marked at Ex.P9 goes to show that, the petitioner was admitted from 24.5.2022 to 3.6.2022..

Hence, during the period of treatment as an inpatient and as an outpatient, the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment,
conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards attendant charges, food, and nourishment and conveyance charges.
30. Another material point of loss of future income is concerned, the petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.

In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate,
with other medical documents.
In the evidence of the PW1, reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him, as per Ex.P5, goes to show that, the petitioner had sustained one simple and one grievous injuries.

To substantiate this,
the petitioner had placed, wound certificate and x-rays for consideration.

Apart from this, another material witness, by name Dr.S.A.Somashekar examined as PW2, whose evidence bring forth for consideration, in connection with the proof of disability sustained by the petitioner, consequent upon the accident.
Apart from this, in connection with his dental injuries, placed the evidence of PW4 Dr. N. Chaithanya.

31. In the evidence of this material witness PW2, deposed that, on the history of RTA, the petitioner had sustained, Grade II liver injury, Right arm fracture of shaft of humerus, fracture maxilla fracture mandible.
In this regard, he underwent ORIF with LC DCP for right humerus and ORIF with mandible and maxilla.

At the time of his examination, on the basis of clinical and radiological examination, and also by virtue of complaints of the petitioner, noticed about wasting of right shoulder griddle and upper limb is seen, surgical scars and keloid are seen over right shoulder and arm, puffiness of right sided face also been seen.
Apart from this, x-ray report shown united fracture shaft humerus with implants in situ.

On the basis of entire evaluation of the disability of the petitioner, this witness had opined that, total disability of right upper limb of the petitioner at 38%
and that of his whole body at 19%.
Further opined that, the petitioner being a mason feels difficulty and the said disabilities will come in the way of his working.
Further, he opined that, the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants which would costs around Rs.40,000/- in private set up.

In support of his evidence produced OPD card and x-ray as per Ex.P15 & Ex.P16.
32.

Another witness PW4 Dr.N.Chaitanya Babu in his evidence deposed that, due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner had got oroacial injuries of pan facial fracture and has got physical orofacial disability and disfigurement with respect to mandibular fracture 20% and total disability is of 20%

Naveen Kumar B.V vs Manjunatha.N on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190638738/
7 with respect to the whole body.

The disability sustained by the petitioner in connection with lower jaw, is permanent in nature, he was treated with plates and screws for his fracture, he requires another surgery to remove the plates which are placed during the surgery.
Though the petitioner will be able to look normal, that is his aesthetics function will become normal, but his ability to bite hard food will be restricted.

In support of the evidence of this witness produced x- ray as per Ex.P19.
33.

At the time of cross-examination of PW2, admitted that, he is not the treated doctor, he has gone through the discharge summary and wound certificate of the petitioner, but not taken any opinion from the treated doctor.
Apart from this, denied the suggestion that, he assessed the disability of the petitioner in higher side.
On the other hand, at the time of cross-examination of PW4 also, admitted that, he is not the treated doctor.

The petitioner had sustained fracture in connection with his jaw,
but no effect caused to his tooth, but he cannot chew hard foods, as he has to bite the hard food in his slow manner.
This witness also denied the suggestion that, he assessed the disability of the petitioner in higher side.
34. Over all appreciation of evidence of PW2 & PW4 along with the entire medical documents the wholebody disability expressed by both PW2 & PW4 seems little bit exorbitant.

Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by both the witnesses, along with the point that,
fracures are united, it is apt to take whole body disability as 15% instead of 19+20=39%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.
35. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 24 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has placed driving licence & Aadhar card marked at Ex.P7 & Ex.P8, for consideration.
On going through the said documents, pertaining to the petitioner, the date of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 24.11.1997.
The accident occurred on 24.5.2022.

Therefore, as on the date of accident,
the age of the petitioner is considered as 25 years.

To the said age as per Sarla Verma case,
multiplier '18' is to be taken into consideration.

36. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in the main petition, and also in the examination-in-chief evidence, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, prior to the accident, he was working as a mason and getting an income of Rs.20,000/- per month.
In support of his avocation, and definite income per month, he has not placed any iota of documents.
In such a situation, as per law, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.

Hence, by keeping in mind about the year of the institution of this case, and also, as per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.15,500/-.
37.

In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.15,500 X 12 X 18 X15/100= Rs.5,02,200/-.
Naveen Kumar B.V vs Manjunatha.N

on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190638738/
8 38.

Next factual aspect loss of amenities is concerned, due to the injuries mentioned in the wound certificate and in other medical documents, and on appreciation of the evidence of the PW2 and PW4, in toto, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood as a mason, by looking into the present condition of the petitioner.
By taking into consideration of all these aspects, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities.
39. In connection with the future medication expenses is concerned, PW2 has stated that, the petitioner requires surgery for removal implants which could cost Rs.40,000/-.
In support of this statement of the PW2, not mentioned any amount or placed estimation, in order to know the approximate cost of the future medical expenses of the petitioner.
On the other hand, PW4 also exprssed, in his evidence that, the petitioner requires another surgery to remove the plates.
But no estimation in this regard, placed for consideration.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of future medical expenses.

40. In view of my due discussions held above, on various aspects, the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
Compensation heads Compensation  amount 1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 70,000-00 2.Loss of income during Rs. 15,500-00 laid-up period and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Rs.2,09,422-00 4. Attendant, Rs. 20,000-00 Nourishment and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Rs.5,02,200-00 due to disability 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 30,000-00 7.
Future medication Rs. 40,000-00  Total Rs.8,87,122-00 41.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,87,122/- (Rupees eight lakhs eighty seven thousand one hundred and twenty two only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

9 award amount.
LIABILITY:
42.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Maruthi Swift car bearing registration No.KA-50- MB-2587, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

As such, it is the strong assertion of the petitioner that, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company, of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
43. As per the records insurance policy was valid from 5.5.2022 to 4.5.2023.
The alleged accident had taken place on 24.5.2022.
This aspect and existence of insurance policy has not been seriously disputed by the other side.
There is no evidence about the violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

44. As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2, being the insurance company and indemnifier has to satisfy the award.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
45.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
*O R D E R*
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

Consequently, the petitioner is entitle for compensation of Rs.8,87,122/- (Rupees eight lakhs eighty seven thousand one hundred and twenty two only),, along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
Expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years.
And remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
